title: The Endless Hymn
premise: Ulyana Brightwater takes a teaching post in the fog-bound town of Hollowmere, where a class of students vanished in 1974 and the school has quietly lost children ever since. When mirrors begin lagging behind reality, Ulyana learns the town's founding families feed something beneath the chapel to keep their own children safe—a bargain renewed every fifty years with a returned offering. Refusing to hand over a new child, Ulyana descends to return what was taken in 1974 instead: the stolen names of the missing class, kept in a lead box by the school's headmaster. The ending costs Ulyana their voice—payment exacted for speaking the names aloud—but frees the lost class, collapses the bargain, and leaves Hollowmere's powerful families facing the thing they starved for half a century.
about_author: Quentin Pemberton is the pen name of a former rural schoolteacher who taught for eleven years in coastal villages before turning to horror full-time. They write in an unheated farmhouse office and claim never to keep mirrors on the premises.

chapters.title: The Long Road In
chapters.summary: Ulyana arrives in Hollowmere by bus through fog that seems to part reluctantly, taking a lodging above the bakery. The town is polite but watchful; no one meets their eyes twice. POV: Ulyana. Emotional beat: cautious optimism curdling into the first prickle of being unwelcome.

chapters.title: Twenty-Six Desks
chapters.summary: At St. Brannoc's School, Ulyana finds their classroom has twenty-six desks but only nineteen students enrolled. A custodian named Merrick warns them not to count out loud. POV: Ulyana. Emotional beat: professional curiosity shadowed by institutional dread.

chapters.title: Attendance
chapters.summary: Ulyana begins noticing gaps: students who appear in registers but never in seats, and one boy, Tomas, who flinches when roll is called. The headmaster, Aldous Vane, deflects questions about 1974 with practiced charm. POV: Ulyana. Emotional beat: the teacher's instinct to protect awakening against bureaucratic stonewalling.

chapters.title: One Second Late
chapters.summary: In their lodgings, Ulyana notices their reflection lags—a blink arriving after the blink. Testing it with a metronome confirms it: every mirror in the house runs one second behind. POV: Ulyana. Emotional beat: rationalist denial cracking into cold, physical fear.

chapters.title: The Baker's Daughter
chapters.summary: The baker's daughter, Ilse, quietly tells Ulyana that her grandmother was in the class of '74 and came back wrong—never spoke again, watched windows at night. She begs Ulyana not to ask questions at school. POV: Ulyana. Emotional beat: loneliness eased by an ally, then chilled by what the ally knows.

chapters.title: What the Town Sings
chapters.summary: On Sunday, Ulyana attends chapel and hears the congregation sing a hymn whose verses don't match any hymnal—and the children sing it flawlessly, as if drilled. Vane conducts. Underneath the floor, something keeps time. POV: Ulyana. Emotional beat: horror dressed in reverence; the sense of a town complicit in liturgy.

chapters.title: Merrick's Ledger
chapters.summary: Custodian Merrick shows Ulyana a maintenance ledger going back decades: every seven years, a classroom sealed, desks removed, a line of payment inked in red. The last entry is dated this year. POV: Ulyana. Emotional beat: betrayal—the school isn't failing these children; it's spending them.

chapters.title: The Founding Families
chapters.summary: Ulyana researches Hollowmere's history and finds six family names recurring since the town's founding—Vane among them—all granted land near the old chapel well. Their prosperity has never once faltered. POV: Ulyana. Emotional beat: the theme of power crystallizing; corruption with a paper trail.

chapters.title: Tomas Is Counted
chapters.summary: Tomas stops coming to school. His desk vanishes overnight. His mother, hollow-eyed, thanks Ulyana for 'not making it harder.' Ulyana confronts Vane and is threatened with dismissal—and something worse, implied. POV: Ulyana. Emotional beat: grief and fury; the price of survival made personal.

chapters.title: Ilse's Bargain
chapters.summary: Ilse reveals her family was offered protection from the counting if she stopped helping Ulyana. She helps anyway, bringing her grandmother's effects: a photograph of the class of '74 with one face scratched out. POV: Ulyana. Emotional beat: love against duty—Ilse choosing loyalty over safety.

chapters.title: The Scratched Face
chapters.summary: Identifying the scratched face leads Ulyana to a sealed parish record: in 1974, the six families took not a child but the entire class's names, written on slips and locked in a lead box, to bind the thing below more cheaply. It has been starving ever since, taking interest. POV: Ulyana. Emotional beat: revelation—the debt is specific, and repayable.

chapters.title: Reflections Talking Back
chapters.summary: The lagged reflections begin acting independently: showing Ulyana the chapel undercroft, a door, a box. The mirror-self mouths words Ulyana cannot read yet. POV: Ulyana. Emotional beat: uncanny alliance; even the haunting wants the debt settled.

chapters.title: Vane's Confession
chapters.summary: Cornered, Vane admits the system: his ancestors built it, his daughter is next unless the offering is renewed properly. He believes he is protecting children, not sacrificing them. He refuses to open the box. POV: Ulyana. Emotional beat: pity entangled with contempt; power corrupting even love.

chapters.title: Sealed In
chapters.summary: Ulyana is locked in the school overnight—Merrick's doing, or so it seems until Merrick slips them a key and the ledger page naming the box's hiding place. Something walks the corridors, counting doors. POV: Ulyana. Emotional beat: terror and an unexpected act of courage from a coward.

chapters.title: The Undercroft Door
chapters.summary: Following the mirror's map, Ulyana enters the chapel undercroft through the old well shaft, finding the class of '74's belongings arranged like an altar, dust undisturbed for fifty years. The air hums with the hymn. POV: Ulyana. Emotional beat: awe tipping into dread at the threshold.

chapters.title: What Waits Below
chapters.summary: In the deep chamber, Ulyana encounters the thing the families fed: vast, patient, shaped by fifty years of hunger into something almost human-shaped from all the taken children. It does not attack. It asks, in many small voices, for its names. POV: Ulyana. Emotional beat: horror transmuting into terrible compassion.

chapters.title: The Lead Box
chapters.summary: Ulyana retrieves the lead box from beneath the chapel floor while Vane and the families arrive to stop them—offering Ilse in Tomas's place. Merrick stands between them and the door. POV: Ulyana. Emotional beat: the climax of power versus conscience; allies paying in blood and nerve.

chapters.title: Reading the Names
chapters.summary: Before the assembled town, Ulyana breaks the seal and reads all twenty-six names aloud. Each name spoken costs a piece of their voice, hoarsening to silence. The chamber opens; the class of '74 steps out of the dark, unaged, blinking at the light. POV: Ulyana. Emotional beat: sacrifice fulfilled; love outlasting duty.

chapters.title: The Reckoning
chapters.summary: Unfed and unbound, the thing turns to the six families who bargained with it. What happens in the undercroft is heard, not seen. Vane survives only because his daughter drags him away, renouncing her name and inheritance. POV: Ulyana, voiceless, observing. Emotional beat: justice rendered without mercy; survival's true invoice.

chapters.title: Aftermath
chapters.summary: Hollowmere buries its dead and burns the hymnal pages. The freed class of '74, fifty years displaced, grieves everyone they've lost. Ilse stays with Ulyana, learning sign language alongside them. POV: Ulyana. Emotional beat: exhausted tenderness; the cost counted honestly.

chapters.title: The Empty Desk
chapters.summary: School reopens. Twenty-six desks stand in Ulyana's room, and for the first time they are all filled—some by faces that shouldn't be possible. Ulyana teaches without speaking, writing lessons on the board, and the children learn. POV: Ulyana. Emotional beat: quiet restoration; purpose remade around loss.

chapters.title: One Second Even
chapters.summary: Months later, Ulyana passes a shop window and their reflection moves exactly in time. In the glass, briefly, twenty-six children wave goodbye. Ulyana waves back, voiceless, smiling. POV: Ulyana. Emotional beat: release; the haunting ends not with banishment but with gratitude.
